cors.hcl_says: infra/modules/demo-api/main.tf justifies the absent cors block: adding allow_origins = ["*"] would turn 'any page may make a request and not read the answer' into 'may read it'
cors.handler_does: app._response, app.py:272, sets access-control-allow-origin: * on EVERY /v1 response including 4xx, 5xx and the 204 OPTIONS
the_real_delta: The written justification is FALSE as deployed: any page can read every /v1 response cross-origin.

The confidentiality delta is ZERO. authorization_type = NONE, no cookie, no Authorization header, no credential of any kind: everything readable cross-origin is already readable by anyone who types the URL.
access-control-allow-credentials is NOT set and the origin is a literal *, so a browser will never attach ambient credentials. There are none to attach.

The preflight is INCOMPLETE, not permissive: OPTIONS returns 204 with access-control-allow-origin: * and NO allow-methods and NO allow-headers, so a cross-origin fetch with content-type: application/json is blocked by the browser.

A CORS SIMPLE REQUEST is not blocked: content-type: text/plain carrying a JSON body reached the handler and was parsed - app._body ignores content-type. Measured: 423 from the guard, i.e. the request arrived. So a third-party page can drive any POST from a visitor's browser. Since the endpoint is unauthenticated this grants an attacker nothing they did not already have, except attribution.
Vary: Origin is absent. Harmless with a constant *; it would matter the day the value became origin-dependent.

cross_domain.W3_dsn: Nothing in the deployment package reads MAINLINE_DEMO_DATABASE - only scripts/deploy/deploy.{sh,ps1} do.
